XXI.|OF THE APOSTLES.|353}}</noinclude>made of al, and falling vpon the necke of Paul, they kissed him, {{verse|chapter=20|verse=38}}† being sorie most of al for the vvord which he had said, that they should see his face no more. And they brought him going vnto the shippe.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XX.}}}}

''16. Pentecost.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Christian Pentecost.}}Though the Apostles might desire to come to the Iewes Festiuities, by reason of the general concourse of people to the same, the better to deale for their saluation and to spred the Gospel of Christ, yet it is like that they now kept solemly the Christian Pentecost or whitsontide, for memorie of the Holy Ghost, and that S. Paul vvent to that Feast of the Christians rather then the other of the Ievves. And Ven. Bede saith here, ''The Apostle maketh hast to keepe the fifteth day, that is, of remission and of the Holy Ghost''. For, that the Christians already kept the eight day, that is, the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Sunday.}}Sunday or our Lordes day, and had altered already the ordinarie Sabboth into the same, it is plaine by the Scriptures ''(1 Cor. 16, 2. Apoc. 1, 10''.) and by antiquitie. ''Iustin. Mart. Apolog. 2 ad Anton. Pium in fine''. And it is as like that they changed the Ievves Pasche and Pentecost as that, specially when it is euident that {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Aug. ep. 118 c. 1''.}}these Festiuities be kept by Apostolike tradition, and approued by the vse of al auncient Churches and Councels.

''29. Rauening vvolues.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Rauening wolues are the Heretikes of al ages.}}The gouernours of the Church are foretold of the great danger that should fall to the people by vvolues, that is to say, by Heretikes, vvhose cruelty tovvard the Catholikes is noted by this terme. They be knowen by the forsaking the vnitie of the Church whereof they were before, by going out and dravving many disciples after them, and by their peruerse doctrine. Such vvolues came afterward in deede in diuers ages, Arius, Macedonius, Nestorius, Eutyches, Luther, Caluin, great bloudsucking vvolues, and vvasters of the flocke of Christ.

''35. It is a more blessed thing to giue.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Christs speaches not written in the Gospel.}}Among many other infinite goodly things and speaches vvhich Christ spake and be not vvritten in the Gospels, this sentence is one: which S. Paul heard of some of the Apostles daily conuersant vvith him, or els learned of Christ him self, or of the Holy Ghost. And it signifieth, that whereas the vvorld commonly counteth him happie that receiueth any benefite, as almes either temporal or spiritual, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Great almsmen blessed.}}yet in deede he that giueth or bestovveth, is more happie. Which if the vvorld did wel consider, men would giue almes faster then they do, if it were but for their owne benefite.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XXI.}}}}}}

{{c|''From Milétum going on his iourney, 4 he can not be dissuaded neither at Tyre, 8 nor at Cæsarea (in both which places the Holy Ghost reueled how he should be handled in Hierusalem, 10 the Prophet Agabus expresly foretelling that the Iewes there should deliuer him to the Gentils) 15 but to Hierusalem he commeth: vvhere being welcome to the Christians, and namely to Iames the Bishop, and to the Priests, while he goeth about to satisfie the Christian Iewes there, who had been misinformed of him as if he had taught it to be vnlawful for the Iewes to keepe Moyses Lavv: 27 he is inuaded by the infidel Iewes, and ready to be murdered by them, vntil the Romane souldiars do rescue him.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, a bearded man.png|imgsize=115px|fl={{verse|chapter=21|verse=1}}}}ND when it came to passe that vve sailed, being caried from them, with a straight course we came to Coos, and the day folowing to Rhodes, and from thence to Patara. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=2}}† And when vve had found a ship that passed ouer to Phœnice, going vp into it we sailed. {{verse|chapter=21|verse=3}}† And when we were in the sight of Cypres, leauing it on the left hand, vve sailed<noinclude>{{rh||Yy|into}}</noinclude>
